title: 002 - Baseball
method: claude-code: written from the transcript, links verified by script

items.name: Baseball
items.description: The episode's game: Nintendo's launch-day NES baseball game, a port of the 1983 Famicom original.

links.label: Baseball (NES, Famicom Disk System) - The Cutting Room Floor

items.name: 10-Yard Fight
items.description: The other NES launch game, covered in the previous episode, also a simple sports title.

items.name: Nintendo Entertainment System
items.description: The console Baseball launched with in October 1985; the hosts also compare it to the Japanese Famicom original.

items.name: Toys "R" Us
items.description: One of the stores where you could pick up the NES at launch.

links.label: Wikipedia: Toys "R" Us
links.note: American toy, clothing, and baby product retailer

items.name: Circuit City
items.description: Electronics retailer another host remembers buying the NES from; the story is saved for the post show.

items.name: Game manuals (NES manual archive)
items.description: The instruction booklet Sam studied for ten minutes to make sense of all the controls.

items.name: Backyard Baseball
items.description: A computer baseball game with a jingle for every batter, which the hosts wish this game had.

items.name: Hit by pitch
items.description: The ball passes straight through the batter in this game, so a hit by pitch never happens.

items.name: Extra innings
items.description: After a tie in the ninth inning this game simply ends instead of playing extra innings.

items.name: Perfect game
items.description: The hosts joke that a perfect game is impossible when you can't control the fielders.

links.label: Wikipedia: Perfect game (baseball)
links.note: Game where at least one team has no baserunners

items.name: MLB (the league)
items.description: The league whose teams the game's single-letter squads are based on.

items.name: New York Yankees
items.description: One of the real MLB teams the game's letter-and-color teams stand in for.

items.name: Detroit Tigers
items.description: Another real team the game's teams appear to be modeled on.

items.name: Philadelphia Phillies
items.description: A real MLB club the hosts spotted among the game's teams.

items.name: Nintendo 3DS

items.name: NEStalgia Essential Games List

items.name: MLB The Show
